title: A doc comment is `///`, and its only tags are `@see` and `@example`
scope:
what marks a comment in *Novis source* as documentation, what may appear inside one, which
tools consume it, and when an undocumented public member is reported. Not in scope: where an
implemented `Core` member's documentation lives, which is
[0117](0117.md) and is unchanged — a
`Core` member is Rust and documents itself in the registry, so it never carries a `///`; the trivia
layer's losslessness property and the `SyntaxIndex`, which are
[0099](0099.md) § 1; the LSP's request set, which is
[0099](0099.md) § 5 and M4B; the website's rendering, which
[website/README.md](../../website/README.md) owns; and Rust's own `///`/`//!` in `crates/`, which is a
different language's mechanism entirely.

summary.headline: A doc comment is `///`, and its only tags are `@see` and `@example`
summary.body:
A documentation comment starts with `///`; four slashes or more is an ordinary comment. Inside
is Markdown prose plus exactly two tags, `@see` naming a member and `@example` naming a file,
and any other `@tag` stops the build. There is deliberately no `@param`, `@return`, `@throws` or
`@var`: the signature already says the first two. The reference, the website and `nvs doc` all
render the one JSON `nvs meta --json` emits. Nothing requires a doc comment by default: `nvs
check --strict-docs` reports a public member without one, and publishing a package turns that
on.
